videos.title: How To Build The Future: Paul Graham & Amjad Masad
videos.description:
Replit was building toward the AI coding era years before it had a name. In 2024, the company shipped an agent that could take a request in plain English, work through errors, provision its own infrastructure, and keep going until the software actually worked. The model companies even reached out to ask how Replit had pulled it off.

Co-founder and CEO Amjad Masad had been thinking about making programming radically more accessible since 2008, and Replit’s original pitch deck predicted AI-generated code before the Transformer paper was published. Today, that same technology is moving into banks, manufacturers, and other large companies, where Amjad says teams are replacing software projects once scoped at $10 million with $250,000 of Replit.

On How to Build the Future, Paul Graham sits down with Amjad to talk about why Replit was so well positioned when coding agents arrived, what comes after vibe coding, and his bigger vision for the “self-driving company,” where AI agents increasingly build and operate the software a company needs.

videos.title: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) EXPLAINED | Everything Is a Plugin
videos.description:
In this video we take a deep dive into DeepSeek Harness (DSH), DeepSeek's open-source agent harness, built on the Cordis plugin system around one idea: everything is a plugin, including the agent loop, the tools, and even the system prompt.

We start with a quick tour of the new Electron desktop application, then break down the architecture of DSH and the history and design of Cordis, the plugin system that powers it. We look at how plugins provide services, how dependency injection and events connect every part of the application, and how Cordis tracks registrations to clean up plugins safely when they unmount.

Then we go hands-on: we write real plugins in code, run `dsh web --patch` with a custom `cordis.patch.yml`, watch three plugins (a greet tool, a bash guard, and a hello plugin) load and fire inside the app, and finish by loading the plugins into the desktop application via npm packages and the `.dsh` user configuration.

By the end, you'll understand how the composability of DSH works and how to create and load your own plugins, including a custom agent loop that never calls a model.

---

- Cordis GitHub repository: https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis

- DeepSeek Harness website: https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/

---

- How the Cordis plugin system powers everything

videos.description:
Will Anthropic make it from filing an S-1 to trading on Nasdaq? Jamin Ball, partner at Altimeter and author of Clouded Judgement, joins swyx to walk through the roadshow, the Thanksgiving window and what investors would need to believe about Claude.

Jamin makes a case for going public that starts with the lenders financing GPU clusters. Then he opens the accounts: in the first half of 2026, Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss and generated $3.9 billion in operating cash. As frontier AI labs expand into applications, where should startups build? a16z Partner Joe Schmidt joins HubSpot co-founder and CTO Dharmesh Shah to explore why the software opportunity is growing, and how founders can stay off the “Yellow Brick Road” the labs are racing down.

Drawing on HubSpot’s evolution, Dharmesh explains why founders should start with a narrow market, learn quickly, and solve the whole customer problem. They discuss where application companies can build lasting value as models become infrastructure: workflows, customer context, and the systems where work happens.

They also explore HubSpot’s AI experiments, the rise of one-person businesses, and why cheaper software creation could unlock markets that previously couldn’t support a software company.

98% of human DNA doesn't build proteins—it controls how our cells work, and holds vital clues to why diseases happen and why 90% of new drugs fail in clinical trials. Understanding the genome at the molecular level is the key to deciphering the blueprint of human life.

In this episode, Professor Hannah Fry speaks with Google DeepMind's Žiga Avsec and Adam Gayoso about AlphaGenome, the AlphaGenome Atlas, and AlphaGenome 2—exploring how AI reads non-coding DNA down to single-cell resolution to pinpoint disease-causing mutations and help researchers solve medical mysteries.

videos.title: AI Realism Workflow the Pros Use (Eleven v4 + Seedance 2.5)
videos.description:
Keep your AI film characters sounding the same in every scene with Eleven v4 and Seedance 2.5.

Create AI Films → https://elevenlabs.io/creative?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=trend_tutorials&utm_content=create_consistent_character_voices_with_eleven_v4_and_seedance_2_5_ai_workflow

One of the biggest problems in AI filmmaking is characters losing their voice between scenes. In this workflow, we walk through how to pair Eleven v4 voice generation with Seedance 2.5 inside ElevenCreative so your character keeps the same voice, emotion, and delivery across every shot. We start by generating the perfect delivery in Eleven v4 using audio tags to direct the performance, then storyboard the scene in Flows with the voice over in place before generating any video.

From there we cover three ways to use that voice generation as a reference in Seedance 2.5, each one making the result more consistent:

• Method 1 • Use the Eleven v4 generation as an audio reference alongside a character reference and a set reference, then prompt the scene with tagged references
• Method 2 • Convert the MP3 into a plain black MP4 video and use it as a video reference, which tends to extract the delivery more reliably than the audio file
• Method 3 • Add a timestamp transcript from the black video using an LLM node, tag it in your prompt, and offset the timestamps so the action (like a crash landing) lands before the character starts speaking

We also cover choosing a voice from the Great voices for Eleven v4 selection in the voice library, lip syncing the generation to your character in Flows, and generating the scene separately so you can control the background. By the third method you can focus entirely on the prompt and the action while the voice delivery stays consistent every time.

videos.title: Turning Stranded Energy Into Intelligence: Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller
videos.description:
Chase Lochmiller runs one of the most operationally complex companies in AI: Crusoe builds power plants, manufactures electrical equipment, operates gigawatt-scale data centers, and runs a managed AI cloud on top, all under one roof. He just closed a round at a $31 billion valuation, and he got there by selling off the Bitcoin mining business that was paying the bills.

Chase explains why Crusoe is modeled on Exxon, not a cloud provider, and why he partners with companies that look like competitors. He makes the case that a company that outgrows the person who got it there is the rule, not the exception, and that CEOs almost always fire too slowly. He also talks candidly about hiring a coach, working hard to become a polished speaker when it didn’t come naturally, and why the data center industry’s biggest problem is a marketing problem.

I meet with a group of Sequoia founder CEOs between 20 and 2,000 employees, and one of them told me his business is becoming dizzyingly complex beneath him. Chase has the clearest answer I’ve heard for how to hold that in your head. 

And yes, we talk about summiting Everest.

0:00 – Introduction
2:12 – The boiling frog: how a founder holds a 2,000-person company in his head
8:16 – DRIs, the weekly staff meeting, and saying it until you're sick of it
11:19 – Urgency at scale: Elon's "change the world or die tomorrow" tension
14:55 – Startups die of suicide, not homicide

videos.title: Confronting Our AI Future: Closing Keynote "Discovery Loop" with Jeff Dean and Fei-Fei Li
videos.description:
This closing fireside chat brings together two of the field's most consequential builders — Jeff Dean, whose work at Google has helped define the modern AI stack, and Fei-Fei Li, whose case for human-centered AI has shaped how the field thinks about who this technology should actually serve. Coming at the end of a day spent grappling with AI's risks and unresolved questions, the conversation turns to where the two of them agree, where they don't, and what they think the choices ahead really come down to.

*Speakers:* 

- Fei-Fei Li: Inaugural Sequoia Professor in the Computer Science Department at Stanford University, and a Founding Director of HAI. She served as the Director of Stanford’s AI Lab from 2013 to 2018. Li has served as a Vice President at Google and Chief Scientist of AI/ML at Google Cloud (2017-2018), board member or advisor in various public or private companies and is currently a Co-founder/CEO of World Labs, an AI company focusing on Spatial Intelligence and generative AI. 

- Jeff Dean: Computer scientist and software engineer. He is best known for his work at Google, which he joined in 1999. He led Google AI from 2018 to 2023 and was Google's chief scientist from 2023 to 2026. Dean co-founded the AI research start-up Discovery Loop in 2026.
